The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md`

Steps:
1. Read `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

1	# vsim Semihosting Investigation
2	
3	> SUPERSEDED 2026-06-09: the vsim -> QEMU2 handback was removed repo-wide; the simulator is now 2-phase (QEMU1 drain -> vsim drain). The QEMU2/handback content below is historical.
4	
5	Scope: can we port QEMU's RISC-V semihosting into the Verilator-based vsim so
6	that binaries linked with `-mvh` (Andes virtual hosting, `libgloss_vh`) can
7	perform I/O system calls on both QEMU and vsim?
8	
9	This document answers step 1 only: how the current vsim handles those system
10	calls today.
11	
12	## Bottom Line
13	
14	vsim does NOT implement semihosting. Every guest syscall trap is fatal.
15	The fixtures work around this with the Phase-2 rule: no libc I/O between
16	`enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
17	
18	## Current vsim Trap Flow
19	
20	1. `libgloss_vh` in the Andes toolchain compiles `printf` / `_write` /
21	   `_exit` / `_sbrk` down to the RISC-V semihosting magic triple:
22	
23	   ```
24	   slli x0, x0, 0x1f    # at mepc - 4
25	   ebreak               # at mepc
26	   srai x0, x0, 0x7     # at mepc + 4
27	   ```
28	
29	2. vsim's hart takes a breakpoint exception at `ebreak` (mcause = 3) and
30	   jumps to `mtvec`.
31	
32	3. `mtvec` points to the fixture's own trap stub:
33	   `tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S:19-120` saves all GPRs/CSRs and
34	   calls `handle_trap()`.
35	
36	4. `tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c:23-52` reads `mcause`,
37	   `mdcause`, `mepc`, `mtval` via inline CSR reads, prints
38	   `[ERROR] Trap occurred!` to stderr through libgloss, then calls
39	   `_exit(mcause)`.
40	
41	Critical: `handler.c` never inspects the bytes around `mepc` to recognize
42	the magic triple. The comment at `handler.c:4-6` admits this:
43	
44	> libgloss_vh routes syscalls through the RISC-V semihosting magic triple,
45	> not through `ecall`, so there is no syscall-dispatch table here. Any trap
46	> is treated as a fatal error.
47	
48	That is why CLAUDE.md and `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:2-9` carry the Phase-2
49	rule: between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` the fixture must not call
50	any libc I/O function. Phase 1 and Phase 3 print fine because both QEMUs
51	are launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`.
52	
53	## Why the Phase-2 Rule Exists in Code
54	
55	- `tests/fixtures/Makefile:22-24` -- comment explaining libgloss_vh
56	  and that "vsim does not implement semihosting."
57	- `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:2-9` -- documents that
58	  inside the span the magic triple would route to mtvec and loop.
59	- `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` -- launches QEMU2 with
60	  `-semihosting-config` so Phase 3 I/O still works.
61	- `verilator/src/main.cpp:114` -- mentions semihosting only as part of
62	  QEMU2 launch docs.
63	
64	Grep across `verilator/` for `semihosting`, `sys_write`, `SYS_WRITE`,
65	`SYS_READ`, `_sbrk` returns no implementation, only those references.
66	
67	## How QEMU Does the Same Thing (Reference)
68	
69	- Detect: `QEMU/target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_privileged.c.inc:28-70`
70	  decodes `ebreak`, reads `[mepc-4, mepc+4]`, matches the triple, then
71	  raises `RISCV_EXCP_SEMIHOST` instead of `RISCV_EXCP_BREAKPOINT`.
72	- Target glue (RV-specific arg/ret regs):
73	  `QEMU/target/riscv/common-semi-target.h:14-26` -- args in `a0/a1`,
74	  return value placed in `a0`.
75	- Dispatcher (around 20 syscalls, ARM Semihosting v2.0):
76	  `QEMU/semihosting/arm-compat-semi.c` and
77	  `QEMU/semihosting/syscalls.c`. Implements `SYS_OPEN`, `SYS_CLOSE`,
78	  `SYS_READ`, `SYS_WRITE`, `SYS_SEEK`, `SYS_FLEN`, `SYS_STAT`, `SYS_ISTTY`,
79	  `SYS_HEAPINFO`, `SYS_EXIT`, `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED`, and more.
80	
81	RISC-V reuses the ARM Semihosting v2.0 spec verbatim via the magic triple;
82	it is not a RISC-V-specific variant.
83	
84	## libgloss_vh / -mvh Details
85	
86	- `-mvh` is an Andes toolchain flag that selects virtual hosting mode,
87	  routing I/O through the semihosting magic triple instead of through
88	  ecall / proxy-kernel.
89	- `tests/fixtures/Makefile:39-44` link order:
90	
91	  ```
92	  RT_C_LIBS := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
93	  ```
94	
95	- `-lgloss_vh` provides `_write`, `_exit`, `_sbrk`, `_read`, ... built
96	  on the magic triple. Source is not in this repo; it ships in the Andes
97	  toolchain.
98	
99	## vsim Host-Side Hooks Available Today
100	
101	There is no DPI-C bridge, SystemC export, or printf-debug channel from
102	guest to host. The only existing guest-to-host paths are:
103	
104	- The DMI bus (Debug Module) that `ResumeDriver` and `StateDrain` already
105	  use to read and write GPRs / FPRs / CSRs / V-state.
106	- The shared `/dev/shm` mmap region (Tier-2 fixtures) -- the host process
107	  can read it concurrently while the hart runs.
108	- `mtvec` running guest code that the fixture itself controls.
109	
110	vsim's main entry is `sc_main()` in `verilator/src/main.cpp`. It uses
111	`spdlog` and `fmt` for host-side logging; the guest cannot reach those.
112	
113	## Two Natural Integration Points for a Port
114	
115	1. Guest-side, in-trap: extend `handle_trap()` in
116	   `tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c` to detect the magic triple
117	   (read bytes at `mepc-4` and `mepc+4`), emulate the syscall, write the
118	   result into `a0` in the trap frame, advance `mepc` by 4, and return.
119	   I/O reaches the host via the existing `/dev/shm` mmap (a tail-reader
120	   on the host turns the mmap region into stdout).
121	   - Pros: zero vsim core changes; isolated to the fixture runtime.
122	   - Cons: needs a mmap-based stdio protocol; harder for `SYS_OPEN` /
123	     `SYS_READ` against arbitrary host files; not the same path as QEMU.
124	
125	2. Host-side, over DMI: the `handoff_controller` watches for the
126	   semihosting exception via DMI (same way it already watches CSR
127	   triggers), pauses the hart, reads `a0..a7` via Abstract Commands,
128	   executes the syscall on the host, writes `a0` back, advances `mepc`
129	   by 4, and resumes the hart.
130	   - Pros: architecturally equivalent to QEMU; full POSIX surface
131	     available; no guest-side runtime changes.
132	   - Cons: needs a new trigger path in `handoff_controller` and a new
133	     syscall dispatcher module under `verilator/src/hybrid/`.
134	
135	Next step (not in this doc): pick one of the two integration points and
136	sketch it end-to-end -- syscall list, register-read order, `mepc` fixup,
137	file-descriptor table.

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andes-sim`

  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals

  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the

  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andes-sim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andes-sim run --model fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).

  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`

  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,

  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /

     through a bogus address).

     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.

     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.

  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.

"source": "## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andes-sim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andes-sim run --model fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--model hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."
